Generate Sensitivity Analysis Plot for Bayesian Meta-Analysis

Source: R/sensitivity_plot.R
sensitivity_plot.Rd

Creates a comprehensive sensitivity analysis visualization showing how meta-analytic estimates vary across different prior specifications, analysis approaches, and publication bias adjustments. Supports all model backends (brms, MetaStan, bayesmeta, rstan, cmdstanr) and integrates RoBMA for bias-adjusted sensitivity analyses.

Usage

sensitivity_plot(
  model,
  data,
  priors,
  measure,
  prior_order = NULL,
  model_order = NULL,
  rob_var = NULL,
  exclude_high_rob = FALSE,
  incl_common_effect = FALSE,
  incl_random_effect = TRUE,
  incl_selection_weight = FALSE,
  incl_pet_peese = FALSE,
  incl_robma = FALSE,
  robma_fit = NULL,
  seed = TRUE,
  add_probs = FALSE,
  null_value = NULL,
  null_range = NULL,
  add_null_range = FALSE,
  color_null_range = "#77bb41",
  label_control = "Control",
  label_intervention = "Intervention",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  title_align = "left",
  xlim = NULL,
  x_breaks = NULL,
  color_palette = NULL,
  color_overall_posterior = "dodgerblue",
  color_overall_posterior_outline = "blue",
  split_color_by_null = FALSE,
  color_favours_control = "firebrick",
  color_favours_intervention = "dodgerblue",
  plot_width = 4,
  font = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted model object (brmsfit, meta_stan, bayesmeta, stanreg, stanfit, or CmdStanMCMC).

data

A data frame containing the study data.

priors

A named list of prior specifications. Each element should be a list with name (display label), mu_prior (a bf_prior object), and optionally tau_prior (a bf_prior object). See bf_normal for constructors.

measure

Character. Effect measure: "OR", "RR", "HR", "IRR", "MD", or "SMD".

prior_order

Optional character vector of prior keys specifying display order. Defaults to the order in priors.

model_order

Optional character vector of section labels specifying display order. Overrides the default ordering.

rob_var

Optional. Name of risk of bias variable (unquoted).

exclude_high_rob

Logical. Include sensitivity excluding high RoB studies. Default FALSE.

incl_common_effect

Logical. Include common-effect model section. Default FALSE. Only applies when the base model is random-effects.

incl_random_effect

Logical. Include random-effects model section. Default TRUE.

incl_selection_weight

Logical. Include RoBMA selection (weight) model rows. Default FALSE. Requires robma_fit.

incl_pet_peese

Logical. Include RoBMA PET-PEESE rows. Default FALSE. Requires robma_fit.

incl_robma

Logical. Include full RoBMA sensitivity rows (conditional and model-averaged). Default FALSE. Requires robma_fit.

robma_fit

A single fitted RoBMA object (from RoBMA::RoBMA()) or a named list of RoBMA objects (one per prior level). Required when any RoBMA option is TRUE.

seed

Integer seed for reproducibility. Default TRUE (uses model seed).

add_probs

Logical. Add probability columns. Default FALSE.

null_value

Numeric. Null value for hypothesis testing.

null_range

Numeric vector of length 2 or single value. ROPE.

add_null_range

Logical. Show null range region. Default FALSE.

color_null_range

Character. Color for null range. Default "#77bb41".

label_control

Character. Control group label. Default "Control".

label_intervention

Character. Intervention label. Default "Intervention".

title

Optional title.

subtitle

Optional subtitle.

title_align

Character. "left", "center", or "right".

xlim

Optional x-axis limits.

x_breaks

Optional x-axis breaks.

color_palette

Optional named vector of colors for sections.

color_overall_posterior

Fill color. Default "dodgerblue".

color_overall_posterior_outline

Outline color. Default "blue".

split_color_by_null

Logical. Color by null. Default FALSE.

color_favours_control

Character. Default "firebrick".

color_favours_intervention

Character. Default "dodgerblue".

plot_width

Numeric. Width ratio for density plot. Default 4.

font

Optional font family.

Value

A patchwork object combining tables and density plots.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
priors <- list(
  vague = list(
    name      = "Vague",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 10),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 1)
  ),
  weakreg = list(
    name      = "Weakly Regularising",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 1),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.5)
  ),
  informative = list(
    name      = "Informative",
    mu_prior  = bf_normal(0, 0.5),
    tau_prior = bf_half_cauchy(0, 0.3)
  )
)

sensitivity_plot(
  model   = fit,
  data    = dat,
  priors  = priors,
  measure = "OR",
  incl_common_effect = TRUE,
  exclude_high_rob   = TRUE,
  rob_var            = rob_rating
)
} # }
